OP, it sounds like you're experiencing one of two things: a manager that does his metrics entirely by "butt-in-seat" time, or your manager is actually paying people different amounts. I'd say either is just as likely without knowing more about your place of work.

Most managers really want some minimum number of hours from each employee no matter how efficient they are... in fact from a productivity standpoint they want their most efficient people working the longest time because that derives the most benefit for the company (did I mention I'm a manager myself, fuck me right?). So a smart (but maybe not nice) manager will push their strongest to do more, even though they are already doing the most, and generally leave their B team picking up the scraps hoping to pawn them off to someone else or lay them off.

So what does this mean for you? You probably won't find a business where you get to do predefined X work efficiently and go home early, and do this day after day, year after year. What you can do is accomplish as much work within the Y hours you are willing to work, push back on your manager if you find yourself doing over 40 hours a week regularly (or 45, or whatever your number is, but probably not much less than 40), and ask for a raise maybe once a year. If you are actually more efficient than your team members, that salary negotiation will probably go well. If it doesn't, you submit your resume to other companies and find someone who will pay you more. There's often a 2x disparity between pay of workers that look similar on the surface except one is a fucking rockstar at their actual work (and has probably changed jobs at least once or twice to get some raises) and the other fucks around on reddit voat all day and doesn't ask for shit.
